_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
Running work keeps mobile work visible and retains finished jobs while others run. The test seeded a conversation at /c/rw-mobile that started two background jobs, "echo ready; sleep 600" and "sleep 601". "The strip" is '[aria-label="Running work"]', "the toggle" is its [data-testid="running-work-toggle"], "the items" is the strip's [data-testid="running-work-items"], "the jobs" are the items' [data-testid="background-job"] elements, and "the scroller" is ".messages-container". The viewport is 390x500.
1. Navigate to /c/rw-mobile and wait up to 30s for [data-testid="message-input"] to be visible.
2. The toggle should come to contain "2 tasks" (wait up to 15s). The toggle's ".running-work-name" containing "echo ready; sleep 600" and the one containing "sleep 601" should both be visible. The toggle must not contain "Running:".
3. The strip's nextElementSibling must have the class "messages-bottom-sentinel".
4. Eval: set the scroller's scrollTop to its scrollHeight. Its scrollHeight - clientHeight - scrollTop should become at most 2.
5. In one eval, as a phone tap does: dispatch a bubbling Event "touchstart" on the toggle, then call the toggle's click().
6. There should be exactly 2 jobs, and the job containing "echo ready" and the job containing "sleep 601" should be visible. This should become true: the strip's bottom (getBoundingClientRect) is greater than the top of its closest ".messages-container" and at most that container's bottom (the opened panel is in view).
7. Click the toggle (a real click). It should have aria-expanded "false".
8. In one eval on the scroller: dispatch a bubbling WheelEvent "wheel" with deltaY -20, then subtract 20 from its scrollTop (the reader scrolls up a little). Then record the scroller's scrollTop in a window variable as the reading position.
9. Eval: call the toggle's click(). The items should be visible, and the scroller's scrollTop should stay within 2 of the reading position (poll until |scrollTop - reading position| <= 2).
10. The job containing "echo ready" should have a [data-testid="background-job-tail"] containing "ready". The items should contain no details or summary elements (count 0).
11. Call "killEcho" (kills the "echo ready" job through the API); it should return "ok".
12. The toggle should come to contain "1 task" (wait up to 15s). The "echo ready" job's ".running-command-time" should have exactly the text "Finished", it should have no [data-testid="background-job-kill"] (count 0), and its tail should still contain "ready". The "sleep 601" job's ".running-command-time" should contain "Running".

steps.expression: (function(){ const s = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); return s.scrollHeight - s.clientHeight - s.scrollTop <= 2; })()
(function(){ const t = document.querySelector('[data-testid="running-work-toggle"]'); t.dispatchEvent(new Event('touchstart', {bubbles: true})); t.click(); return 'done'; })()

(function(){ const strip = document.querySelector('[aria-label="Running work"]'); const container = strip.closest('.messages-container'); const stripRect = strip.getBoundingClientRect(); const containerRect = container.getBoundingClientRect(); return stripRect.bottom > containerRect.top && stripRect.bottom <= containerRect.bottom; })()

(function(){ const s = document.querySelector('.messages-container'); s.dispatchEvent(new WheelEvent('wheel', {deltaY: -20, bubbles: true})); s.scrollTop -= 20; window._readingPos = s.scrollTop; return s.scrollTop; })()
